findings.reason: The original standalone tiles have no figure. The explicit two-face geometry, five seam arrows and reversed face boundaries materially clarify the concrete witness and its integral five-orbit relation, so an explanatory schematic is warranted under the expanded diagram scope. This is an editorial illustration addition, not a missing proof.
findings.action: Added two opposite regular pentagons with ten vertex labels, paired seam labels and orientation arrows in final Remarks; explained the translations, vertex quotient, rotation action and cellular boundary.

correction: Added a final Remarks illustration of the double-pentagon translation gluing. Original carrier is preserved byte-for-byte as a prefix, including the full statement and proof; all frontmatter is byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Upper primitive pentagon with vertices V_k=cL zeta^k; lower primitive pentagon with vertices -V_k, indices modulo five. Display uses the same rotation and scale on each and a separate centre offset.
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 5.1 gives W_+=cH and W_-=-cH; step 3.1 gives the regular pentagon vertices. A common nonzero similarity preserves the parallel sides and all translation pairings. The picture contains five explicit full side segments and five vertex dots per face, including explicit last-to-first sides.

Direct substitution gives tau_k(V_k)=-V_{k+1} and tau_k(V_{k+1})=-V_k. Derivative 1 preserves tangent vectors. Each upper side k is labelled e_{k+1} and points V_k to V_{k+1}; the paired lower arrow points -V_{k+1} to -V_k and has the identical label, as required by step 5.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: All ten vertices identify to p_infinity.
diagram_math_checks.check: The two adjacent pairings send V_i to -V_{i+1} and -V_{i-1}; hence upper indices differing by 2 identify. Since 2 generates Z/5Z, all upper vertices and thus all lower vertices identify. This agrees with the infinity-chart endpoint identification in steps 2.1 and 5.1.

diagram_math_checks.orientation: Upper face boundary +sum_j e_j; lower face boundary -sum_j e_j.
diagram_math_checks.check: The upper arrows run counterclockwise; lower arrows run clockwise while both complex-coordinate faces have counterclockwise positive boundaries. Step 2.1 has y_+ increase and y_- decrease on positive disk boundary arcs. Therefore the displayed face boundaries produce d_2(a,b)=(a-b)(1,1,1,1,1), d_1=0, and the single H_1 relation sum_j e_j=0 exactly as in step 6.1.

diagram_math_checks.action: T_0 rotates both faces by zeta, sending e_j to e_{j+1}.
diagram_math_checks.check: Multiplication by zeta sends V_k to V_{k+1} and -V_k to -V_{k+1}, so the seam indexed k+1 advances to k+2, consistently on both faces. This is the rotation statement of step 5.1 and edge action of step 6.1.
